piece_type: Exhibit booth panel (“Hemady Conference Banner”); also reported via FDA Bad Ad Program

cases.heading: False or Misleading Risk Presentation
cases.claim: “HEMADY® reduces up to 80% of the number of tablets required for a therapeutic dose of dexamethasone for the treatment of adults with MM” | “Hemady® is a unique strength dexamethasone tablet bioequivalent to five 4 mg tablets of dexamethasone”
cases.context: Exhibit panel with efficacy claims and no risk information; PI has multiple W&Ps.
cases.rationale: Entirely omits risk information, creating a misleading impression about safety.
cases.check: Rule: any piece with product claims (incl. convention banners/panels) must contain risk information.

cases.heading: False or Misleading Claims about Efficacy
cases.claim: “REAL-WORLD COMPARISON OF ADHERENCE to Hemady® and generic dexamethasone among patients with MM”
cases.context: Retrospective claims-data cohort (data on file): inconsistent MM confirmation between arms, NDMM/RRMM mixed, no covariate control, n=43 vs n=3,775, possible double counting.
cases.rationale: Study design/methodology cannot support comparative adherence conclusions.
cases.check: Judge: RWE/claims-based comparative claims; flag unbalanced arms, no covariate adjustment, unverified diagnosis selection.
